workflow: lab data analysis, choice of tool
quote: IMO neither programming languages nor Excel are a great fit for data analysis. Something purpose-made, like JMP or even GraphPad, is probably the better choice in most situations.
problem: Neither Excel nor code fits lab data analysis; grad students can't be supported on scripting and Excel has quirks
need: A purpose-built analysis tool that keeps the data visible like a spreadsheet but runs proper statistics without requiring programming

workflow: omics, lightsheet microscopy and MRI data in a small academic lab
quote: This grad or postdoc is then charged with running some statistical analyses without any training whatsoever in data science. What is an outlier anyway, what do you mean by “normalize”, what is metadata exactly?
problem: Untrained grad students/postdocs are assigned the lab's statistics and do not know what outliers, normalization or metadata mean
need: Explain outliers, normalization and metadata in plain language at the point of use, inside the analysis workflow

quote: So in this context I hope all of you can appreciate that ANY help in bringing some real data science into mom-and-pop laboratories would be a huge huge boon. And please god, let it be FOSS.
problem: Small labs have no data-science support and little budget
need: A free, open-source analysis tool usable by small labs without dedicated data staff

quote: data they'd collect from experiments would be thrown out selectively so that they could publish better curve-fits.
problem: Points are silently dropped to make curve fits look better
need: Record every excluded point with a reason and show exclusions on the fit and in the report so selective removal is visible

quote: Another requirement was that samples had to be blindly randomized before we analyzed them, so that nobody could manipulate the analytical process to get their desired result.
problem: Analysts who know group labels can steer the analysis
need: Offer a blinded mode that hides group labels and randomises sample order until the analysis is locked

role: researcher using computers as a research tool (stated)
quote: 3. Retain raw data files. 4. Retain files produced in the course of analysis. 5. Retain custom source code. 6. Version control all the above.
problem: For mostly physical experiments, what matters is keeping raw data and every analysis file, more than re-running code
need: Keep raw data, each analysis step and its outputs together in one versioned project file

quote: there isn't any other software that allows them to easily do whatever they need to do with the data, quickly iterating on the ideas AND then present it nicely.
problem: Biologists stay in Excel because no other tool lets them iterate quickly and also present the result nicely
need: Combine spreadsheet-speed iteration with publication-ready graphs in one tool

quote: there aren't good GUI tools for entering them anyway, and it leads to countless errors that maybe (here I speculate) they just assume will wash out as noise.
problem: Clinical researchers hand-type non-tabular data into Excel grids because no GUI exists for structured entry
need: Provide structured data-entry tables with typed columns and validation instead of free grids

quote: They insist I give them p-values or something they can present as though they were p-values. ... Then they throw out all the nuance in the data, put one asterisk for p < 0.05, two asterisks for p < 0.01, etc.
problem: Results get reduced to asterisks; nuance and effect sizes are lost
need: Show exact P values next to effect sizes and confidence intervals by default; make star-only summaries an explicit opt-in

quote: My PhD worked on bigger data than could be analysed in the regular biological sciences way (excel + stats software), so I learnt R.
problem: The usual Excel + stats package route could not handle the data size
need: Handle data sets larger than spreadsheet limits without forcing the user to learn a programming language

quote: Compare this to python, where they have to go the unix shell set up the environment, load the libraries. When they come back reset everything and get back to where they started.
problem: Environment set-up and session loss make Python hard for biologists
need: Zero-install environment that keeps the session and data state between visits

quote: I re-wrote the process in AWK, and was able to complete the data-reduction task in about 60 seconds on a DEC 5000 workstation. But my numbers did not match the spreadsheet results, and finding out why was an interesting process.
problem: Re-implementing the lab's spreadsheet data reduction gave different numbers
need: Document every computation step so results can be reproduced and reconciled across tools

quote: I am more interested in understanding well the specific steps they take computationally and in a sensitivity analysis of their computational portion (if you slightly alter your binning threshold do you still get that fantastic clustering?).
problem: Readers can't tell whether results depend on arbitrary analysis thresholds
need: Make it easy to re-run an analysis across a range of thresholds/parameters and report how robust the result is

quote: most wet lab scientists treat you more like a resource, a grad student they need to make their pvalue or figure panel pop nicely
problem: Wet-lab scientists outsource p-values and figure panels to an analyst
need: Let bench scientists produce their own correct statistics and publication figure panels

quote: And if you were that wet lab person and wanted to present a figure that the statistician generated, you would learn everything about the test used, and all the assumptions made when choosing that method of analysis over others.
problem: Wet-lab people present figures without knowing the test and its assumptions
need: Attach the test used, its assumptions and why it was chosen to every result and figure

quote: By learning VIM and unix commands I can do data analysis 1000x quicker on my experimental work than other scientists in my department, just because they are busy fooling around with MS Excel/Origin/LabView.
problem: Colleagues lose time in GUI tools for repetitive analysis
need: Batch-apply the same analysis to many files without manual clicking

quote: the data is stored in a convenient way for humans to read, but impossible to process via a script (think patches of columns in separate excel sheets, sometimes the labels are on the side of the value instead of on top).
problem: Lab data is laid out for human reading (scattered column blocks, side labels) and can't be processed
need: Import messy human-layout sheets and convert them to a tidy table, or guide entry into an analysable layout from the start

quote: Example: using a non-parametric "U"-test when a parametric "T"-test gave a non-significant result. Along with low numbers of replicates.
problem: Tests are swapped after the fact to reach significance, with few replicates
need: Fix the test choice from the design before results are shown, and log any later change of test

role: bioinformatics postdoc / medical research data analyst (stated)
quote: They would never ask us to commit fraud, only perhaps to "double check" an analysis 10 times until it shows what they want to see.
problem: Analyses are re-run repeatedly until they give the wanted answer
need: Keep an analysis history showing how many variants were run, so forking paths are visible

quote: At some point Excel and Origin weren't dealing well with ever increasing data sizes in my field (biology).
problem: Excel and Origin could not cope with growing biology data sizes
need: Stay responsive with large data sets in a point-and-click tool

role: former member of an academic department (stated)
quote: One professor used to hunt around for different statistical tests until she found one which gave her the desired p values so she could publish.
problem: Test shopping for a desired P value
need: Recommend the test from the data design up front and flag when several tests were tried on the same comparison

quote: I think some of it is Rstudio the ide, which shows variables in memory on the side bar, you can click to see them. It makes everything really accessible for those that aren't programmers. It seems to replace excel use for generating plots.
problem: Biologists adopt tools that show the data alongside the analysis
need: Always show the underlying data table next to the analysis and graph, clickable

quote: Just today I am working on a qPCR array (yes people still use those) with one "housekeeping" gene replicated 4 times for ddCt normalization. 80 miRs go up, none go down, out of 400. No one sees any problem with this, the data is the data.
problem: ddCt normalization against one unstable housekeeping gene produces one-directional changes nobody questions
need: For ΔΔCt, check reference-gene stability and warn when nearly all targets shift in the same direction

quote: if a collaborator sends data for analysis where the sample size was too small for the effect, or worse, asked to find statistical differences between 1-2 samples per group, you can't fix that with any amount of algorithmic mumbo-jumbo.
problem: Analysts are asked to test differences with 1-2 samples per group
need: Warn when n per group is too small for the chosen test and show the power/detectable effect

quote: The number one thing that most biologists need (that most scientists need) is a basic understanding of statistics when doing experimental design.
problem: Experiments are designed without statistical reasoning; replicates get added late if at all
need: Plan replicates and power before the experiment, inside the same tool used for analysis

quote: My goal as a computational biologist isn't to do work for or correct biologists who don't understand statistics, it's to get biologists tools to do this kind of work easily on their own and bridge the gap in understanding.
problem: Biologists depend on computational staff for routine statistics
need: Tools that let biologists do routine statistics correctly on their own, with explanations

quote: The reason is its strong tendency to fail silently (and, with RStudio, to frequently keep going even when it does fail.) As a result, people get garbage results without realizing
problem: Analysis software continues after errors and yields plausible-looking garbage
need: Fail loudly: stop and explain when inputs or computations are invalid instead of returning numbers

quote: As a computational biologist who uses R I am often frustrated by experimental colleagues who use Excel and often can't remember how they transformed the data months later.
problem: Point-and-click transformations leave no record
need: Every point-and-click step should generate a visible, saved log or code of what was done

quote: If you don’t know what you’re doing, it’s very easy to misapply existing statistical tests
problem: Life-science PhD students without maths/code background misapply tests
need: Guide test choice from the design and check assumptions automatically

quote: I've watched life science people spend months manually clicking boxes in the tools they have, because they don't have a developer embedded in the team to write some 10-liner automation scripts.
problem: Life-science teams spend months on manual clicking for repetitive analysis
need: Templates/batch re-run so the same analysis applies to new data without re-clicking

role: consultant to chemical and materials companies (stated)
quote: Things like being able to dynamically re-group/nest variables and recalculate statistical tests, dual axis capabilities, automatic sig fig number reformatting, just all kinds of quality-of-life features
problem: BI tools lack scientific interactive plotting; Python needs code maintenance
need: Interactive regrouping that recalculates tests, dual axes and automatic significant-figure formatting

role: consultant to chemical and materials companies (stated)
quote: The only programs that really get the aesthetics of scientific plotting right without a ton of customization are JMP, Origin, and Igor Pro (props if you’ve heard of it), but these are all desktop apps
problem: Good scientific plot defaults exist only in desktop apps
need: Publication-quality scientific plot defaults in a browser tool

quote: Their main figure lacks errors bars. ... The lack of error bars across the paper make me think they didn’t do any technical replicates, which is also a problem.
problem: Figures without error bars hide variability and missing replicates
need: Default graphs that show individual points and error bars, and require stating n and replicate type

quote: It seems like something that would serve the scientific community by allowing people to program complex processes and handle images procedurally. ... I don't know anybody that likes using ImageJ.
problem: ImageJ is disliked; procedural image pipelines are hard
need: A friendlier, node/procedure-based image quantification pipeline whose outputs feed the analysis

workflow: EC50 titration curves, many curves at once
quote: For example I work with bio folks measuring "EC50" values, basically parameters of titration curves in a wet lab. It seems like a simple curve fitting problem with say 5 parameters. But then these wet lab scientists measure hundreds of curves at once
problem: Hundreds of EC50 curves are fitted independently though they should share structure
need: Fit many dose-response curves together with shared/global parameters and report per-curve EC50s with uncertainty

workflow: open lab notebook, HPLC, PCR, gels
quote: Sometimes, the lack of tooling to do this makes it harder (ever tried to export an HPLC trace and then convert it to a format so that you can view it on a web page?).
problem: Instrument outputs (HPLC traces) are hard to export into viewable formats
need: Import common instrument export formats directly and render them

quote: Zero friction (which benchling doesn't have yet) reporting is an absolute must. Run a PCR? Ok, that run gets uploaded to the notebook and filed in the correct experiment.
problem: Recording each run is high-friction so it gets skipped
need: Auto-attach instrument runs and their analysis to the right experiment with no manual filing

workflow: SEM, XRD, PL spectra; Origin projects
quote: handle messy data in originlab. Me and (mostly) opus have made some mcp tools for opj files (i hate these) covering batch fitting, peak decomposition, waterfall plots and plot export
problem: Origin .opj project files are hard to work with; batch fitting needs custom tooling
need: Open/convert Origin project files and batch-fit many spectra

quote: Those are "dynamite plots", a favorite of scientists, but the statisticians I know prefer to use boxplots or dotplots instead.
problem: Scientists default to dynamite plots
need: Default to dot/box plots with all points; make bar+error a deliberate choice

quote: We should have cameras that can establish that published images have not been modified (or at least provide raw and adjusted pairs
problem: No way to show a published image was not altered
need: Keep raw and adjusted image pairs linked to the quantification

quote: And electronic notebooks I've used tend to be even more annoying than paper (too rigidly formatted and not adaptive to workflow optimization but it's difficult to explain).
problem: ELNs are too rigid for real lab workflows
need: Flexible record structure that adapts to the lab's workflow

quote: Apparently I saved hours of retyping for one person who was doing a manual JOIN on gene names between two CSV files. As in ctrl+f name of gene from file A, copy, paste into another window. For thousands of rows.
problem: Researchers merge tables by manual find/copy/paste
need: Built-in merge/lookup of two tables by an identifier column

quote: all their statistics were calculated by hand using approximate equations which were supposed to make it doable using a simple calculator. ... Going back in old records, my wife found that there were a lot of errors in the recorded results.
problem: QC statistics done by hand with approximations produced many errors for decades
need: Ready-made QC/validation statistics that compute exactly from entered results

quote: I don't have chunks of time large enough to quiet my mind, frame-shift, and work on my research at the code level.
problem: Clinician-researchers lack time blocks to work at code level
need: Analysis that can be done in short sessions without coding

quote: Select all, format cell before pasting data into a sheet should work as expected. However, formatting is ignored as soon as anything is pasted into the spreadsheet.
problem: Pre-set text formatting is lost on paste, so gene names still convert
need: Pasted data must keep the column type the user set; never auto-convert identifiers

quote: whenever I get an xlsx file, I just learnt to always check for dates, it is sometimes possible to get around this if there are other identifiers or genomic coordinates, but some gene names will be converted to the same date, which leaves it impossible to backtrack the original genename.
problem: Date conversion is irreversible when two genes map to the same date
need: Detect likely gene-name-to-date conversions on import and warn

role: partner of a research group member (stated)
quote: They don't want to have a dozen different tools that they have to switch between fifty times an hour, converting data in the meantime, they want to know one or two very well and have the data all there.
problem: Switching between many tools and converting data costs time
need: One tool holding the data, analysis and graphs together, no export/import loop

quote: It is super hard to figure out a way to import data into excel without triggering auto-conversions. ... because Excel is fundamentally untrustworthy.
problem: No easy way to import CSV without auto-conversion
need: Import that preserves values exactly unless the user asks for a type

quote: the typical result of trying to teach them better tools is the experimentalists just rolling their eyes and saying that they don't have time to learn some nerdy program because they have experiments to run.
problem: Bench scientists won't invest time in learning new tools
need: Near-zero learning curve: familiar spreadsheet-like entry, results without training

role: worked on statistical methods in biology research (stated)
quote: I do think that less emphasis on "fancy" statistics, and more emphasis on simple data visualizations and common sense analyses would be a good thing.
problem: Pressure for fancy statistics beyond biologists' training
need: Lead with simple data visualisation and plain analyses before advanced methods

quote: identifiers in the form of "1E123" get turned into scientific numbers. ... Those things are sneaky: you can have thousands of rows, and Excel/LO doesn't mind if only the 0.1% matches its rules for smartness. They just change without notice, leaving the others intact.
problem: A tiny fraction of IDs silently become numbers
need: Treat ID columns as text and report any value that would change on import

quote: This shit could be avoided if they had a "scientific mode" to not be smart with your data, and be the default mode for any file in CSV/TSV mode.
problem: Spreadsheets have no 'don't touch my data' mode
need: A default mode that never alters imported values

quote: I had to use Excel for 100% of my publications and posters in medical services research. ... While I'd love to use only R, most of my collaborators wouldn't be able to use it
problem: Collaborators can't open R work, forcing Excel
need: Share analyses in a format collaborators can open without installing software

role: computer-savvy member of a lab collaboration (stated)
quote: I send them some data in CSV, that when opened in Excel turned 123.456 into 123456 (it was a problem with locales, some people using "," as decimal and some using "."). ... A small quantity of numbers bumped up by a factor of 3 could fly under the radar, and distort further measurements.
problem: Decimal-separator locale mismatch silently multiplies values by 1000
need: Detect decimal/thousands separators explicitly on import and show a preview

quote: I am envisioning something with double-entry data checking, enforcement of data types, and rules to check validity.
problem: Spreadsheets lack data-entry validation for science
need: Typed columns, double-entry checks and validity rules in the data table

workflow: PIs/lab techs looking at their data
quote: Not every lab tech or PI can or should learn Python/R/your favorite scripting language, and frameworks like Galaxy take time to set up and maintain, etc etc. Our job is to meet the users where they are
problem: Lab techs/PIs won't learn scripting; Galaxy is heavy
need: A no-setup tool lab techs and PIs can use directly

quote: it's easy to miss it's happening when it happens to a really small subset of genes you are importing into an excel sheet.
problem: Conversions on few rows go unnoticed
need: Highlight changed cells on import

role: author of a biochemical journal article (stated)
quote: we had a 96-element datatable (12x8) and limited space in our biochemical journal article. We were looking to graphically show differences in orders of magnitude to help explain the assay. A 3d column chart fit the bill
problem: No compact plate-layout visual for 96-well results spanning orders of magnitude
need: Plate-map heatmap view with log colour scale for 96/384-well data

quote: Just because you can put a dataset in and get values out - even values that look significant, it doesn’t mean they are - did all of the assumptions and requirements of the methods/tests you used hold true/pass with your data?
problem: Easy GUIs give results without checking assumptions
need: Check and report assumptions for each test automatically, with guardrails

quote: You can press F2 on a cell and visually see what data is being pulled into the function, and you can easily manually check that that single calculation is accurate by re-creating that calculation by hand
problem: Users trust calculations they can trace by hand
need: Let users click any result to see the exact inputs and intermediate values

quote: Even if you do specify a column as a text excel WILL assume that it contains dates sometimes. Happened to me multiple times, even when i set each cell as a text. Seems like copypasting a tab separated values resets the cells to their default state.
problem: Copy-pasted TSV resets text formatting and dates appear
need: Paste must respect the column type already set

quote: To the majority, the unpaired T-Test is the only test that is needed. Ever. Doesn't matter if you have one or two tails, paired or unpaired trials, normally distributed population or skewed.
problem: Unpaired t-test used regardless of design
need: Ask about pairing, tails and distribution before suggesting a test

quote: In academic biology, statistics is routinely considered an afterthought. In the eyes of many labs/PIs, their results are already real. You just have to do those damn statistical tests so the editor will get off your back.
problem: Statistics done only to satisfy editors
need: Make the statistics step quick and integrated so it is done properly rather than as an afterthought

quote: If in your data you find that A has no statistically significant effect, but B does have a statistically significant effect, this does not automatically show that B has, with statistical significance, more effect than A. To do that you have to do a statistical test on the difference in the effects.
problem: Comparing significance labels instead of testing the difference (interaction)
need: When two effects are compared, run and report the interaction/difference test, and warn against 'significant vs not significant' comparisons

quote: On the flipside, I've seen experiments where they are showing that one population of neurons is 2% more dynamic than another population, and sometimes you just wonder if that really matters at all (or if you are really sampling the population well enough)
problem: Tiny effects reported as findings without considering magnitude or sampling
need: Report effect size with CI beside P, and flag small effects

quote: Most authors do not test the statistical assumptions made in the literature and copy the statistical techniques used previously.
problem: Methods are copied from prior papers without checking assumptions
need: Check assumptions on the user's own data even when they pick a 'standard' test

quote: There are as many quantitative microscopy techniques as there are lab teams in the wild. Everyone builds their own correlations depending on their research dive of interest. ... I think feature richness is key (even if 80% of users only need 20% of counting techniques).
problem: Microscopy quantification is idiosyncratic per lab
need: Flexible image-quantification exports that drop straight into the analysis tables

quote: Things like no embedding of vector graphics and no good embedded spreadsheet solution.
problem: ELN cannot embed vector graphics or a usable spreadsheet
need: Export vector graphics and tables that embed cleanly in ELNs

quote: I ran into the limitation of 64K characters per entry. It’s handled by trimming html off the end then autofixing broken stuff. It works so well that it took me a while to figure out why the number of rows was decreasing as more rows were filled out.
problem: ELN silently truncated table rows
need: Never drop data silently; warn on any size limit

quote: I'm an immunologist, and it feels impossible for me to keep on top of my field of research and just about anything else.
problem: No time to learn software practices alongside the science
need: Tools that need no maintenance or coding upkeep from the scientist

quote: The quality is so bad that I think a huge proportion of published results are plain wrong due to bugs in the analysis.
problem: Bugs in ad hoc analysis code produce wrong published results
need: Validated, tested analysis routines instead of one-off scripts

quote: The standard solution is this software package that lets you open each .jpg file one by one (there is a folder with hundreds), and you draw little rectangles and it tells you the average brightness inside. You write the number down inside an excel spreadsheet one by one, alt-tabbing back and forth.
problem: Blot quantification is manual: open each image, draw a box, retype the number
need: Batch densitometry with exported values going straight into the analysis table

quote: I simply need the figure in the minimal amount of time and with the least mental bandwidth, so I can focus on the science and catch the conference deadline. Origin is a very "over-engineered" piece of software, but hey getting a broken axis is so simple
problem: Broken axes need hacks in matplotlib
need: One-click broken axis with unequal segment widths

quote: matplotlib is simply too disappointing for making publication quality figures. The most recently encountered problem is how to plot with a broken x-axis, which is one of the most basic need in physical science but requires a non-trivial amount of hacking to get with matplotlib.
problem: Free plotting tools make basic publication needs (axis breaks) hard; Origin licence lost after university
need: Free tool with built-in axis breaks and publication defaults

quote: I have already enough frustration dealing with my samples, so I simply want the least frustration from the software I use to plot.
problem: Plotting software adds frustration on top of experimental work
need: Minimal-friction plotting with sensible defaults

quote: I was relying on OriginLab (a scientific version of Excel) for my data analysis and it was a real pain.
problem: Origin painful for exploratory analysis
need: Exploratory analysis that is interactive and recordable

workflow: reading old data files on Linux
quote: 2) Extract data from OriginPro worksheet (no viewer for Linux)
problem: OriginPro data trapped in a Windows-only format
need: Import proprietary analysis project files on any OS

quote: But in many cases we don't even have this and people use Fiji to scroll through the z-dimension with a slider. For presentations people often render a movie with Matlab, investing hours to get it right.
problem: 3D image data explored with a slider; presentation movies take hours
need: Easier 3D exploration and export for presentations

quote: I want to be able to take a stack of 100 TIFs, look for a few white spots on a black background - and track their centroids. That's it.
problem: Simple spot tracking requires heavy or outdated tools
need: Simple tracking with CSV export into the analysis tool

quote: Most of my peers either use Excel, blindly learn by rote a series of 'voodoo' commands to input into a very specific program running on a dusty old Win98 machine. Get out a calculator.
problem: Peers rely on rote steps on old dedicated PCs or calculators
need: Accessible, current tool for routine computations on tracked data

quote: "The screening of two subsets of compounds for antiviral activity (Supplementary Fig. 2a and Supplementary Fig. 4b) was performed in a blinded manner, whereas all other experiments were performed in a nonblinded manner."
problem: Most experiments are analysed unblinded
need: Support blinded group labels during analysis

quote: Also the pricing puts this program directly at the range of Graphpad's Prism, which is widely-used in academic fields other than the field of statistics, and quite intuitive.
problem: Price is a key comparison point for statistics/graphing tools
need: Offer Prism-level ease of use at a lower or no price

quote: I did some processing in an afternoon, including writing a python script, that a postdoc had used a month doing manually in Excel.
problem: A month of manual Excel work for what a script does in an afternoon
need: Automate repetitive transformations without coding

quote: I teach people to be very sceptical of excel in my stats courses, for example (aside from some showstopping bugs and downright dangerous defaults, its RNG is particularly crap).
problem: Excel defaults and RNG unreliable for statistics
need: Validated statistics with documented methods

quote: Some researchers are never going to use anything other than Excel for this even when people like me harp on them to stop treating Excel as a database. It's "good-enough", so it gets used more often than it should.
problem: Excel is 'good enough' so it stays
need: Be as immediate as Excel to win adoption

quote: I offered some "Programming for Biologists" courses, to teach people like me to do programming in this way, because it would be much less "dry" (pd.read.excel().barplot() and now you're programming). So far, wherever I offered the courses they said they prefer to teach programming "from the base up".
problem: Teaching starts from abstractions rather than biologists' own tables
need: Teach analysis starting from the learner's own spreadsheet and plots

quote: It's harder to shy away from a very low p-value, even when you know the sampling may not be appropriate.
problem: Very low P values from large data tempt over-interpretation
need: Show sampling caveats and effect sizes alongside tiny P values

workflow: gene list handoff to pathway tool
quote: And if the next step is "yeah, that looks fine - I'll just copy the top 100 genes into this convenient GUI pathway analysis tool", you're suddenly exposed to whatever Excel did to your data.
problem: Copying results via Excel into other GUI tools corrupts data
need: Export clean gene lists directly without passing through a spreadsheet

quote: Besides, the writing process for papers includes sending drafts and spreadsheets to doctors and pathologists and editors, who are probably on hospital computers with a short whitelist of programs
problem: Collaborators on locked-down hospital PCs can only open whitelisted programs
need: Browser-based sharing that needs no installation

quote: At some point, I started using matplotlib + Latex + science plots and it caught on, mostly because there's no need to shift all the data around to a separate programme.
problem: Moving data into a separate plotting programme is friction
need: Plot where the data and analysis already live

quote: Colours are one of the subtle things I so often find difficult to get right.
problem: Choosing colours is hard
need: Good default palettes (colour-blind safe) for scientific figures

role: tool developer in a high-throughput screening lab (stated)
quote: After several years of iterations I can say that so far electronic lab notebooks never worked; there are even several commercial software available.
problem: ELNs fail in HTS lab practice
need: Lightweight records that fit lab practice

quote: To underscore how terrible ELN was at our site, many managers instructed their reports to keep traditional paper notebooks, photograph each page, and upload to an ELN entry.
problem: Pharma ELN so poor that paper was photographed into it
need: Fast, reliable record-keeping software

quote: Then they work to find a subset of the data and a statistical test that gives them a significant result. ... Proper statistics, where you decide on the test you'll apply and on what data before doing the experiment, is almost unheard of.
problem: Subset and test chosen after seeing results
need: Pre-specify the comparison and test before data entry; log deviations

quote: I just saw a paper published in Science had to issue a revision because they found a bug in their analysis code after publication that changed most of their downstream analysis.
problem: Bug in analysis code changed most downstream results
need: Tested analysis routines with cross-checks

quote: Excel is still the easiest way to look at tabular data, even if it isn’t part of the production workflow. And sadly, even if you save the file as txt, Excel would always mangle certain fields.
problem: Even saving as text, Excel mangles fields
need: Easy table viewer that never alters values

quote: All the GUIs I have seen are really not up to the task for typical scientific data. They are clunky, heavy, slow, and difficult to use for visualisation.
problem: Data GUIs are clunky and slow for scientific data
need: Fast spreadsheet-like view with quick visualisation

quote: He was looking at the neuronal response to smells that they gave the rats and had a few signals to match up. ... He was having a hard time getting through all the data in his MatLab code
problem: Aligning multiple signals in hand-written code overwhelms grad students
need: Tools that align/time-sync multiple recorded signals without custom code

quote: I did wet and dry work in my PhD and before, and found a paper notebook to be incredibly inconvenient. Finding things, referring to things, including data or code - all very laborious if it's even effective.
problem: Paper notebooks can't link data, code and figures
need: Link raw data, analysis and figures in one searchable record

quote: One thing we're trying in my program right now is to introduce "Statistical Thinking" as a mandatory class for both wet lab and computational students, to cover the why of statistics and try to teach people how to think about what they're doing, before they hit the "When X, do Y to collect p-value." stage.
problem: Students learn recipes before reasoning
need: Explain why a test applies, not just which button to press

quote: my experience is that folks in that field are much more careful with statistics than in, say, molecular biology labs, but it varies from lab to lab. My PI is exceedingly meticulous about stats -- for instance, we don't report p-values, but rather entire distributions
problem: Molecular biology labs less careful with statistics
need: Show full distributions rather than single P values
